response.explanation: userPermDenialCacheKey builds the key as namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent. The fields are joined with '_', which can appear in Grafana resource names, folder UIDs and user UIDs. Two different checks can therefore produce the same key. For example, name="a_b" with parent="c" and name="a" with parent="b_c" both give "..._a_b_c". When one check is denied, Check stores the key in permDenialCache. Check consults that cache first and returns Allowed=false for the other check without evaluating permissions. This is a fail-closed false denial, not an access grant. The key also shares the ".perm_<uid>_<action>" prefix with the permission-map key, which makes collisions and confusion easier.

response.explanation: userPermDenialCacheKey builds namespace.perm_<uid>_<action>_<name>_<parent> with a plain '_' separator. A name or parent that contains '_' can produce the same key as a different pair. For example, name "a_b" with parent "c" and name "a" with parent "b_c" both give "..._a_b_c". Grafana UIDs and resource names can contain '_'. An empty name or parent shifts the fields in the same way. Check() returns Allowed=false straight from permDenialCache.Get on a key hit, before any permission evaluation. The wrapped caches share one underlying cache and the key has no type prefix. Because of that, a denial cached for one resource also denies a different resource that maps to the same key.
